messages:
maria: Ran nsys inside a k8s pod to profile a KV-cache/batching perf regression. Works on baremetal but inside the pod nsys fails to write trace_marker: 

[error]
ERROR: could not initialize library: cannot open /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/trace_marker: Permission denied

Anyone hit this with nvidia-container-toolkit + runtimeClass?

ryan: That looks like seccomp / capability restrictions. Did you try securityContext.capabilities add SYS_PTRACE or CAP_SYS_ADMIN?

maria: Tried SYS_PTRACE, still can't write to trace_marker. Setting privileged: true fixes it but we can't run all inference pods privileged. Also nsys needs access to /dev/nvidia* devices.

lee: For GPU access you need hostDevices or deviceRequests. Also the toolkit creates sockets in /var/lib/nvidia-container; if perms are wrong it falls back. Example pod snippet: 
```yaml
securityContext:
  privileged: true
containers:
- name: profiler
  resources:
    limits:
      nvidia.com/gpu: 1
hostDevices:
- path: /dev/nvidia0
- path: /dev/nvidiactl
```

devx: Another pattern: run a privileged sidecar (small image) that runs nsys/perfetto and writes captures to a shared EmptyDir, main container stays unprivileged. Less blast radius.

maria: Important note: when I attach nsys the runtime switches kernel selection from CUTLASS to a generic kernel and latency doubles. Timeline shows nsys inserting synchronizations. That changes batching heuristics / warmup and triggers KV cache misses.

ryan: Right — profiler hooks add synchronization points. For less interference use sampling mode or Nsight Systems capture-range=instrumentation to limit the capture window.

maria: Timeline excerpt: 
```
GPU timeline:
0.0ms memcpyHtoD
1.2ms launch conv_cutlass::fprop
1.25ms cudaEventSynchronize (nsys)
1.3ms launch generic_conv
```
You can see the sync in between causing fallback.

lee: Also check node-level file permissions: /var/lib/nvidia-container owned by root:docker with 0700 prevented the toolkit socket from being used. When toolkit falls back, driver paths change and kernels may be different. Seen this on older node images.

maria: Repro script I used (quick): 
```bash
kubectl run -it --rm --restart=Never --image=nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:11.8-base --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"t","image":"nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:11.8-base","securityContext":{"privileged":false},"resources":{"limits":{"nvidia.com/gpu":1}}}]}}' tracer -- bash -lc "nsys profile -o /mnt/out/trace --trace=cuda sleep 2"
```

infra-bot: Created INF-7821: investigate nvidia-container-toolkit permissions on node images + trace node pool suggestion.

devx: Workaround until infra fixes it: provision a small trace node pool with a more permissive seccomp profile and allow privileged pods only on that pool. Mount host /sys/kernel/debug into the pod if okay with security.

maria: Observed KV cache hit rate drop after attaching trace: from ~96% to ~65% briefly which changes batching decisions (small batches, more full forwards). Need to quantify how much of the regression is due to profiler interference vs toolkit perms falling back.

ryan: Could be eviction due to context switches or the driver switching memory paths. Add a microbenchmark: run steady inference, attach/detach tracer, measure kvcache hit rate and kernel selection counts.

lee: I'm going to run that on staging on a node with 5.15 kernel and the current toolkit. Will test privileged sidecar vs privileged main vs host-mounted debugfs.

maria: Pushed a minimal repro + logs to gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/maria/nsys-k8s-perms-pro repro and a short perfetto capture. Please try and paste results here.

devx: :thumbsup:
